info.title: Microsoft Planetary Computer Pro - GeoStats
info.description:
GeoStats: raster-derived statistics over STAC-discovered data.

Submit geometries and a raster collection, receive analytics-ready tabular
output. See
docs/data-plane/design/geostats/how-it-works/geostats-api-design.md for the
rationale behind the resource model, and
docs/data-plane/design/geostats/how-it-works/geostats-design.md for the
underlying algebra.

put.description:
Create or replace a saved computation definition.

This operation stores and validates the definition synchronously. Use the
`run` action to execute it asynchronously.

x-ms-error-code.description: String error code indicating what went wrong.

delete.description:
Delete a computation definition.

Returns `204` on success and `404` if the record does not exist. Runs of
the definition are not touched: a run is a separate resource with its own
lifetime, and its results stay addressable after the definition it came
from is gone. Deleting the parent collection removes its definitions,
formulas, and run snapshots.

204.description:
The computation record was removed.

Deletion is separate from cancellation. A cancelled computation keeps its
record so that `Canceling` and `Canceled` are observable and so that the
partial results already written remain addressable; deletion is what
disposes of it.

post.description:
Run a computation.

Always asynchronous: returns `202` with an `operation-location` header,
following the long-running action contract for an existing resource.
There is no synchronous path and no `Prefer: wait`, because a caller must
handle the asynchronous contract regardless and a second path that
sometimes applies would double the client contract without removing either
branch.

Input and output arguments belong to this invocation rather than the
saved definition. The service generates the run and status monitor id.
Each submission starts a new run, as with ingestion runs. Clients must
not automatically retry submission after an ambiguous failure.

202.description:
The run was accepted and is executing in the background. This is the only
outcome: there is no synchronous path, so a caller implements one contract
rather than two.

operation-location.description:
Url of the status monitor, which is the catalog's operations record at
`/operations/{operationId}`.

retry-after.description: Seconds to wait before polling the status monitor.

get.description: List run operation monitors, including runs of a deleted definition.

post.description:
Plan a run without executing it. Features are filtered and partitioned,
and the STAC search bounded by each partition's envelope, exactly as the
run would do for the given observation strategy. The operation's
additionalInformation reports feature, item and pixel counts, and how
many compute partitions are predicted to be too large to compute as
requested. No raster is read and no result is published. The prediction
comes from measured per-pixel costs; it is not a price or duration. Each submission creates a new operation; clients must
not automatically retry after an ambiguous failure.

code.description: One of a server-defined set of error codes.

BandCommonName.description:
Canonical band name from the STAC EO extension.

Band names in expressions are common names rather than asset keys, so
`(nir - red) / (nir + red)` resolves against whichever bands a collection
declares and the same request works against HLS, Sentinel-2 and Landsat
unchanged.

The union is open because two extension versions are in circulation and a
catalog holds both: EO v1.1 nests `common_name` inside `eo:bands`, while EO
v2.0 moves bands to the STAC 1.1 core `bands` construct as `eo:common_name`
and extends the vocabulary. The members below are the v2.0 set, which is a
superset of v1.1.

BufferSpec.description:
Distance to grow the geometry by before reduction. Omit the buffer entirely
to reduce over the geometry as drawn, which is what analytics usually wants.

The distance must be positive. The buffer is applied in the raster's CRS
after reprojection, so the distance is always metres: naming the property
for its unit is what keeps that from being a silent correctness bug on a
geographic CRS.

BuiltInIndex.description:
Built-in spectral index. The library is the on-ramp rather than the
destination: callers who need their own formulas use `expression`.

values.name: NDRE
values.description: Normalised difference red edge.

values.name: BSI
values.description: Bare soil index.

Calculation.description:
One inline derived band. An expression is required; built-in indices are
reserved and currently rejected.

name.description:
Output column name. Caller-controlled so that output schema does not
depend on expression text.

expression.description:
Band arithmetic over names bound by `bandMapping`, for example
`(nir - red) / (nir + red)`.

Parsed with a restricted AST allowlist and lowered to the canonical
graph. The parser is not the security boundary; structural validation of
the lowered graph is.

bandMapping.description:
Map this formula's expression names to physical assets or bands.
For example, `red` can bind to asset `B04`, and `nir` to band index 4 of
asset `image`. Overrides take precedence over EO common-name resolution
for this formula only; sibling formulas may bind the same name differently.
Each run snapshots these bindings together with the expression.

ComputationCalculation.description:
Exactly one of an inline calculation (name and expression) or a formulaId
referencing a saved formula in the same collection. Formula references cannot
be combined with inline fields or band-mapping overrides. Each run snapshots
the current expression and its band mappings.

name.description:
Output column name. Caller-controlled so that output schema does not
depend on expression text.

expression.description:
Band arithmetic over names bound by `bandMapping`, for example
`(nir - red) / (nir + red)`.

Parsed with a restricted AST allowlist and lowered to the canonical
graph. The parser is not the security boundary; structural validation of
the lowered graph is.

bandMapping.description:

Each run snapshots these bindings together with the expression.

featureBbox.description: Bounding box the STAC search was bounded by, taken from the features.

featureIdentity.description: How output rows will be keyed back to input geometries.

degradation.description:
Resolution coarsening that would be applied to bring the computation
within budget, surfaced before it happens silently.

ComputationRunAcceptedResponse.description:
The run was accepted and is executing in the background. This is the only
outcome: there is no synchronous path, so a caller implements one contract
rather than two.

DataBandReference.description: One physical band bound to a name used in calculations.

assetKey.description: STAC asset key on each matched item.

bandIndex.description:
1-based band index within a multi-band asset. Mutually exclusive with
`bandName`. Omit both selectors for a single-band asset.

bandName.description:
Name declared in the asset's STAC band metadata. Mutually exclusive with
`bandIndex`.

source.description: Catalog to resolve the collection against. `self` only for P0.

filter.description:
CQL2-JSON predicate selecting STAC items for computations and estimates.
Combined with the URL's collection, datetime, and feature bounds. This is
distinct from input.features.filter, which selects analysis geometries.

DegradationPlan.description: Graceful degradation rather than outright rejection.

evaluatedResolution.description: Resolution the computation would actually run at.

FeatureCollectionSource.description:
Where the input geometries come from. Exactly one member must be set.

Supply inline GeoJSON or a catalog asset. Inline collections contain 1 to
100 features, inclusive. The entire JSON request must be smaller than
10,000,000 bytes. Arrow attachments are not supported.

stacAsset.description:
A GeoParquet or vector asset already held on a STAC item in this catalog.
The only unbounded tier: the planner reads its feature count, CRS, and
bbox from file metadata without decoding geometries.

filter.description:
CQL2-JSON predicate over top-level properties in the feature source.
The selected rows define the geometries included in the computation.
This is distinct from `dataSource.filter`, which selects STAC items.

geoJson.description:
Inline GeoJSON FeatureCollection, bounded to a small number of features.
RFC 7946 fixes GeoJSON to WGS 84 longitude and latitude, so this is the
one source whose CRS may be assumed rather than declared.

geometryIdColumn.description:
Column holding the caller's stable identifier, carried verbatim into
every output row. Omit to identify geometries by their ordinal, in which
case results are returned in that same order by default. That ordinal
matches the order supplied only for inline `geoJson`; a `stacAsset` is
stored re-sorted by ingestion, so name a column here to join results
back to the rows the caller knows.

geometryColumn.description: Reserved; currently rejected. Geometry uses the source's default geometry column.

FeatureIdentity.description:
How output rows are keyed back to input geometries.

`column` is preferred whenever the caller has a business key, because it
survives resubmission, reordering, and partial resubmission. `positional` is
for callers who have no such key and do not want to invent one.

values.name: column
values.description: Keyed by a caller-named column, carried verbatim into every output row.

values.name: positional
values.description:
Keyed by the zero-based ordinal of the geometry as supplied. Stable only
within one submission: sending the same file with rows in a different
order produces different identities.

buffer.description:
Optional buffer applied to every geometry during computation. The
candidate-pair estimate does not apply buffers.

Formula.description: A reusable calculation owned by the collection in the URL.

id.description: Assigned from the URL. When supplied, must match the formula id.

description.description: Human-readable description of the formula. Does not affect computation.

expression.description: Band arithmetic for this reusable calculation.

GeoJsonFeature.description: One RFC 7946 feature supplied inline for a GeoStats computation.

GeoJsonFeatureCollection.description: Inline RFC 7946 FeatureCollection accepted by the GeoStats REST API.

GeoStatsComputation.description:
A saved computation definition.

Durable and re-runnable: the definition is what a caller names when asking
for the same analysis again, so re-running last month's work does not mean
re-sending its whole body. Execution state lives on `ComputationRun`.

plan.description: The most recent plan produced for this definition.

links.description:
Links to the operations available on this definition, following the same
shape as the STAC `links` array used elsewhere in this catalog's API.

GeoStatsComputationEstimateRequest.description: Search, geometry and observation inputs needed to plan and cost a run.

dataSource.description: Datetime search in the URL's collection, with an optional CQL2-JSON filter.

input.description: Input geometries and reduction mode used for the estimate.

observationStrategy.description:
The run's observation strategy. Defaults to per-item results. `mosaic` and
`all` read one window around every feature in a partition for every scene,
so they reach capacity with far less area than per-item reads.

temporal.description:
The run's temporal settings. Requires `mosaic` or `all` and a bounded
datetime. The period decides how many scenes are combined at once.

GeoStatsComputationRequest.description:
A GeoStats computation.

Every field maps onto exactly one primitive's arguments, so that exposing a
composable process graph later is a generalisation of this shape rather than
a breaking replacement.

id.description: Assigned from the URL. When supplied, must match the computation id.

dataSource.description: Time range and bands in the collection identified by the URL.

observationStrategy.description: How observations are combined. Defaults to per-item results.

temporal.description:
Optional binning for `mosaic` and `all` observation modes. When omitted,
those modes reduce the whole datetime range as one period. Not valid with
`item` mode.

calculations.description:
Derived bands. A single pass evaluates all of them, so requesting fourteen
indices does not mean fourteen passes over identical pixels. A calculation
may instead reference a saved formula in this collection. References are
resolved on save and on each run; deleting a referenced formula makes
subsequent runs invalid until the definition or formula is repaired.

imageChips.description:
Ordered expressions encoded as bands in a cropped COG stored in the
`image_chips` binary result column. Each chip covers the bounding box of
the geometry being analyzed without masking pixels outside the geometry.
The analytical mask still applies to statistics but does not blank chip
pixels; its raw `fmask` or `scl` band can be included as another chip
expression. Supported for `item` and `mosaic` computations; `all` is
rejected because several observations can contribute at each pixel.
Each row's chip is limited to 1,048,576 bytes, both decoded float32
pixels across all bands and encoded COG bytes. Oversized chips are null;
statistics and their status are unchanged. Chips are not resized.

GeoStatsComputationRunRequest.description: Input and output arguments supplied for one execution of a computation.

output.description: Persistence target. Omit to publish GeoParquet in the default collection.

GeoStatsOperation.description:
Long-running operation record, mirroring the catalog-wide operation shape so
that a GeoStats submission is polled exactly like a catalog write.

This is the status monitor. `operation-location` points at
`/operations/{operationId}`, the catalog's existing record, rather than at a
geostats-specific monitor that would project the same fields under a second
URL. The status vocabulary is that record's own, which is why it reads
`Pending` where the Azure guidelines say `NotStarted`.

creationTime.description: The UTC time at which the operation was created.

startTime.description: The UTC time at which the operation was started.

finishTime.description: The UTC time at which the operation finished its execution.

collectionId.description: Collection the run was attributed to.

statusHistory.description: Every status the operation has passed through, oldest first.

additionalInformation.description:
Per-partition counters maintained while the run executes: `TotalItems`,
`TotalPendingItems`, `TotalSuccessfulItems` and `TotalFailedItems`,
carried as strings by the catalog-wide operation record.
Estimates instead report, after successful completion: `FeatureCount`,
`ItemCount` and `FeatureItemPairs` (their product); `EstimatedPixels`,
feature-item overlap pixels summed over every scene; `PartitionCount`;
`EstimatedReadPixels`, raster pixels the run's windows read;
`MaxScenesPerPeriod`; and `PartitionsOverCapacity`, partitions predicted
to be too large to compute as requested. When it is non-zero, reduce the
scenes per period, the geometry size or spread, or use `item` mode.

GeoStatsStatus.description: Execution status, matching the catalog-wide operation status vocabulary.

ImageChipBand.description: One band in the COG embedded in each result row.

name.description: GeoTIFF band description and position in the requested band order.

expression.description:
Band arithmetic evaluated against raw raster values. The analytical mask
does not blank chip pixels, and its raw band may be requested here.

MaskBitField.description:
One field of a bit-packed mask band.

A one-bit flag needs no `classes`: naming the bit names the class. A wider
field has several states that must be named, and omitting them is an error
rather than a guess.

offset.description: Zero-based offset of the field's lowest bit.

classes.description: State name to value, required when `length` exceeds 1.

MaskClass.description:
A pixel class a mask can reject or keep.

The named members are canonical concepts, and each collection binds them to
its own encoding, which is what makes one request portable: `cloud` reaches
whatever the legend calls cloud, whether that is a bit of HLS `Fmask`, a bit
of Landsat `qa_pixel`, or a class of Sentinel-2 `SCL`. A concept a legend
cannot express contributes nothing rather than failing.

The union stays open because a collection's own class names are data it
publishes rather than vocabulary this API owns. Those pass through verbatim,
including `field:class` for one field of a bit-packed band, as in
`aerosol_level:high`.

values.name: nodata
values.description: Fill: outside the swath, or otherwise not imaged.

values.name: saturated
values.description: Detector saturated or defective.

values.name: cloud
values.description: Cloud, at whatever confidence the product reports.

values.name: cirrus
values.description: Thin or high cirrus.

values.name: cloudShadow
values.description: Shadow cast by cloud.

values.name: adjacentCloud
values.description: Dilated, or buffered adjacent to cloud.

values.name: snow
values.description: Snow or ice.

values.name: water
values.description: Water, where the product flags it. Not rejected by `clear`.

MaskSpec.description:
Validity mask. Kept distinct from a conditional expression because the
planner must see validity in order to perform nodata-aware reduction and to
estimate valid-pixel counts when costing.

Exactly one of `exclude` or `include` must be set.

The service ships no product knowledge. A mask band's legend comes either
from this request or from the STAC classification extension the item
publishes, and this request wins. Hard-coding one collection's class values
would carry a silent copy of someone else's product specification, wrong the
moment they revise it and useless to anyone with proprietary data.

asset.description: Asset holding the mask band. Required with `classes` or `bits`.

classes.description:
Legend for an enumerated mask, where the whole pixel value is one class,
as Sentinel-2 `SCL` is. Maps a class name to its value. A value this
legend does not name is rejected rather than assumed valid.

bits.description:
Legend for a bit-packed mask, where independent fields occupy bit ranges,
as HLS `Fmask` and Landsat `qa_pixel` are. Mutually exclusive with
`classes`.

exclude.description: Classes to reject, keeping every other pixel.

include.description:
Classes to keep, rejecting every other pixel. Applies to enumerated masks
only: naming one field of a bit-packed mask says nothing about the others.

MosaicPriority.description: Pixel priority when overlapping observations form a mosaic.

ObservationMode.description: How observations are combined before their pixels are reduced.

values.name: item
values.description: Keep each STAC item independent. This is the default.

values.name: mosaic
values.description: Resolve overlapping observations into one image.

values.name: all
values.description:
Retain every observation in the reduction, forming an observation cube
over the whole datetime range or within each temporal bin.

ObservationStrategy.description: How observations contribute to the computation.

values.name: item
values.description: Keep each STAC item independent. This is the default.

values.name: mosaic
values.description: Resolve overlapping observations into one image.

values.name: all
values.description:
Retain every observation in the reduction, forming an observation cube
over the whole datetime range or within each temporal bin.

priority.description: Required when `mode` is `mosaic`; invalid for `item` and `all`.

OperationStatusEntry.description: One transition in an operation's status history.

OutputH3Resolution.description: Coarse H3 resolutions that avoid high-cardinality result directories.

OutputPartitioningSpec.description: Optional physical partitions used to prune a large result dataset.

OutputSpatialScheme.description: Supported spatial index for assigning each feature to one home cell.

OutputSpec.description: Where and how results are persisted.

location.description:
Path results are written to, relative to the catalog's configured sink.

A OneLake shortcut points at a fixed path, so a caller who wants one asks
for the same location on every run and creates the shortcut once. The
service does not register or validate the location, so a caller who
changes their calculations and reuses a location gets a Delta schema
evolution rather than a rejection.

stacCollectionId.description:
Collection the completed result is registered into as a STAC item, whose
asset points at the written table and whose properties carry the run's
provenance. Defaults to the raster collection in the computation URL,
not the collection holding an input feature asset.

This is what persists results "directly into the customer's GeoCatalog":
a result is then discoverable through the existing STAC search under the
authorization the catalog already enforces, rather than through a second
registry. Row-level addressing is deliberately not offered; a STAC item
describes an asset, not the features inside it.

partitioning.description:
Hive-style dataset partitioning. Each feature is assigned to one H3 home
cell; polygon intersections with other cells do not duplicate fact rows.

ordering.description:
Row order in the written table. Ordering by feature is a sort, not an
inherent property, so it is the caller's choice rather than a silent one.

OutputTemporalGranularity.description: Supported temporal partition columns for a large result dataset.

RasterResampling.description: Resampling applied to continuous raster bands during grid alignment.

RasterSource.description:
Catalog the raster collection is resolved against.

`self` is the only value for P0: a computation resolves rasters from the
GeoCatalog it runs in. Open Planetary Computer imagery reaches a customer
through ingestion by reference, which makes it an ordinary local collection.

ReducerName.description:
Named reducer. In addition to the named members, `percentile_N` requests the
Nth percentile, where N is an integer from 1 through 99. The set is an
allowlist rather than a caller-supplied callback: an unclassifiable reducer
cannot be checked for decomposability, which would destroy the pixel-budget
estimate and with it limits and admission.

ReferenceGrid.description:
The CRS, resolution, and origin the computation is evaluated on. Explicit
rather than inferred: geometries reproject to the raster's CRS, rasters are
not reprojected.

ResourceLink.description: A hypermedia link to a related resource or an available operation.

method.description: HTTP method to use. Defaults to `GET` when absent.

type.description: Media type of the target representation.

ResultOrdering.description:
Row ordering of a result set.

Execution partitions by scene, so results are naturally produced in
completion order rather than input order. Restoring input order is
therefore a sort, not a free property.

values.name: featureOrder
values.description:
Ascending `featureIndex`, then timestamp, calculation, and statistic.
This is the default, and is what makes omitting an identifier column
usable.

`featureIndex` is the row's ordinal in the geometries as GeoStats read
them. For inline `geoJson` that is the order supplied, so results can be
zipped straight back onto the caller's dataframe. A `stacAsset` is
stored re-sorted by ingestion, so there the ordinal is a stable key for
joining results to each other, not the caller's original row number --
supply `geometryIdColumn` to carry an identifier that is.

The cost is that writing cannot begin until enough partitions have
completed to emit the lowest outstanding index.

values.name: arrival
values.description:
Rows are written as partitions complete, in no guaranteed order. Fully
incremental, and the consumer keys on `featureIndex` or `geometryId`.

SpatialMode.description:
Zonal aggregates the pixels within a polygon; sample extracts a value at a
point. These are different operations with different parameters, and
conflating them is how two callers get different numbers from one request.

StacAssetReference.description: A reference to an asset on a STAC item.

TemporalGridPolicy.description: How temporal analysis handles scenes whose native raster grids differ.

values.name: strict
values.description: Reject a temporal bin unless every scene has exactly the same grid.

values.name: reproject
values.description: Align each scene to the earliest scene's grid before combining it.

TemporalSpec.description:
Temporal binning. The period is the unit of output: a year requested at
`P1W` yields 52 rows per geometry per calculation per statistic, whether or
not any given week held usable imagery.

period.description:
ISO 8601 duration, for example `P1D`, `P1W`, or `P1M`. Omit to reduce the
whole datetime range to a single period.

minValidFraction.description:
Fraction of the geometry that must carry valid pixels before a value is
reported, for example `0.9` for "only if 90% of the field was clear".

Deliberately per geometry per period rather than a property of the item:
a scene-level `eo:cloud_cover` of 20% says nothing about whether the
cloud sat over this particular parcel. Periods that miss the threshold
still produce a row, with `status` of `belowValidFraction` and the
measured `coverageFraction` so a consumer can apply a different rule
without recomputing.

gridPolicy.description:
Handling for scenes on different native grids. Defaults to `strict`.
`reproject` uses the earliest intersecting scene in each period as the
destination grid.

resampling.description:
Resampling for continuous bands when `gridPolicy` is `reproject`.
Defaults to `nearest`. Categorical masks always use nearest-neighbor.

values.name: area
values.description: Edge pixels contribute in proportion to the area inside the polygon.

WriteMode.description: How a computation writes into its output location.

ApiVersionParameters.name: api-version
ApiVersionParameters.description: The API version to use for this operation. Required on every GeoStats route.

ComputationListQuery.name: createdAfter
ComputationListQuery.description: Return only definitions created after this instant.

PageQuery.skip.name: skip
PageQuery.skip.description: Number of records to skip. Defaults to zero.

PageQuery.top.name: top
PageQuery.top.description: Maximum records per page. Defaults to 100.
